#120363. How to Make Sure an 'Onion' Site on the Dark Web Is Legitimate

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1026 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

How to Make Sure an 'Onion' Site on the Dark Web Is Legitimate

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1026 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the dark web isn't just for illicit activities.
  • But this also provides perfect cover for criminals and hackers who create clones of legitimate dark web sites to steal sensitive data and cryptocurrency from privacy-conscious customers.
  • Thankfully, Tor Browser already has a cryptography-backed feature that can verify the authenticity of an onion site, by confirming whether it has end-to-end encryption and extended validation certificates.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the dark web isn't just for illicit activities. In fact, many legitimate online platforms maintain a ".onion" domain on the dark web for privacy reasons, including media outlets like ProPublica and BBC News, social media sites like Facebook, and privacy-conscious communication platforms like Proton Mail and SecureDrop.

But this also provides perfect cover for criminals and hackers who create clones of legitimate dark web sites to steal sensitive data and cryptocurrency from privacy-conscious customers. And given that onion links are long and jumbled, it’s easy for users to accidentally click on the wrong link and end up on a fake website instead of the real one. When the FBI seized 276 onion addresses during 2014's Operation Onymous, they found that 153 of them were phishing sites.

Thankfully, Tor Browser already has a cryptography-backed feature that can verify the authenticity of an onion site, by confirming whether it has end-to-end encryption and extended validation certificates. Here's how this feature works, where it falters, as well as what other red flags you should look for.

According to recent reports, while phishing on the dark web works as it does on the clear web, scammers have a few unique advantages due to the secretive nature of the environment. Most importantly, you can’t just glance at an onion link to tell if the site is genuine. Normal website URLs tend to be short and memorable, while onion links are 56-character strings of alphanumeric text that look mostly like gibberish.

Industry observers note that when you try to connect, Tor Browser verifies the URL against the originating website’s cryptographic key, which is how you know nobody has hijacked the address or tampered with it midway. But since this has the unwanted effect of making domains harder to recall, scammers have a much easier time generating lookalike addresses or creating website clones.

For example, many popular websites use “vanity prefixes” to make their onion addresses more easily identifiable or to add some branding appeal. That means their 56-character onion link starts with something like “facebook,” “bbcnews,” or “ciadotgov.” But scammers can use a free tool like mkp224o to generate lookalike addresses with the same vanity prefix as the legitimate website, which gives consumers a false sense of security.

Of course, most dark web users don’t type addresses directly into Tor Browser; they use dark web directories like the Hidden Wiki to find useful onion sites relevant to their search. Scammers will create fake search engines or link directories to point users to their fake websites, like when the Ahmia search engine discovered that a copy of its platform was directing users to 255 cloned services back in 2015.

Industry observers note that of course, it’s possible to orchestrate phishing attempts that don’t involve cloning sites at all. Researchers at Freie Universität Berlin describe a sophisticated technique where attackers serve the real website through their own reverse proxy, which lets them manipulate parts of the site or log your online activity without your awareness. In 2019, ESET even found a trojanized version of Tor Browser that replaced Bitcoin addresses on websites to direct payments to hackers. So both genuine websites and your browser itself are also vulnerable to manipulation if you download or access them from an unverified source.

There are a few best practices to avoid phishing attacks when using the dark web. None of them are foolproof on their own, but together, they considerably lower the risk of ending up on a fake or manipulated website.

Sources indicate that the Tor Project has a feature called Onion-Location, which lets clear web websites advertise that they have a dark web version available for consumers who prefer more privacy. If opening a regular TLS-backed website using the Tor Browser reveals a purple “onion available” button in the address bar, you can click on it and be redirected to the official onion link associated with that site.

Recent findings suggest that on the desktop version of Tor Browser, you can access an onion site using a shortened version of its URL called an Onion Name. For now, this feature only works with SecureDrop, so newsrooms can establish tip lines with addresses like mysitename.securedrop.tor.onion, which would then redirect to the 56-character original onion address. This feature is in active development, so more platforms might support it in the future.

It has been revealed that when you load up an onion site using the Tor Browser, you’ll see an onion icon on the address bar, which confirms that your connection is end-to-end encrypted. But you can also click on the onion icon to check if the site has an Extended Validation (EV) certificate, which tells you that its authenticity has been verified by a trusted certificate authority like DigiCert. While not every legitimate onion site will have an EV certificate, famous ones like Facebook tend to.

Recent findings suggest that on the other hand, if you see a caution sign next to the onion icon, that means the site is using a self-signed or expired certificate that isn’t guaranteed by a trusted authority. It may also imply that the site is being served over an insecure URL. This doesn’t definitely tell you it’s a phishing site, but it’s a red flag to watch out for nevertheless.

Industry observers note that don’t rely on search engines, link directories, Reddit threads, or Telegram channels too heavily on the dark web. Once you’re sure you’ve found the onion address for a genuine site, bookmark it so you can access it directly the next time you want to visit.

If you realized that you’ve been the victim of a phishing attempt, the first step is to close the browser window with the fake site and access the real onion address to reset any account passwords you may have accidentally divulged.

According to recent reports, also, generally try to enable two-factor authentication and PGP logins on any dark web account that supports it for added security. And if you downloaded Tor Browser from anywhere other than the official Tor Project site, uninstall it now and grab a fresh copy from the official address.

Is there something going on today? A lot of talk about committing crimes and the like, I just can't quite put my finger on why… Ah well, couldn't be key or interesting. What is interesting, however, is Keepsake County, a "midwestern stealth game" that has rolled out on this inauspicious day about stealing stuff from "hideous farmhouses in the middle of nowhere.".

Sources indicate that with the sarcastic intro out the way, I will address the elephant in the room: Vovly's Adventure: Reslimed is out today too. Fine, fine, yes I know GTA 6 is the game everyone's talking about, but Forward Instinct, the devs behind Keepsake County, seem well aware of that in their launch day post for the game: "Folks, thanks for your incredible patience. Keepsake County is finally OUT! And yes, it is deeply ironic that it wound up being today, of all days, that we got the green light to finally release, but here we are.".

According to recent reports, keepsake Country was supposed to release earlier this month, but seemingly got caught up in the backlog Valve are faced with that's undoubtedly been caused by genAI games. In any case, the burgle-em-up does look quite delightful. I'm not sure if I can quite put my finger on exactly why I get this feeling, but it calls to mind a more complex version of the kind of game you'd find on Cartoon Network's website back in the day (which is a high point of praise, I'd like to be clear).

Each house in Keepsake Country is procedurally generated, meaning you never quite know what to expect when you enter. There's lockpicking, resident tie upping, and of course stealing to be done, but it doesn't just stop at the house. Parking your car, for instance, is an crucial thing to consider; do you want it hidden so you're less likely to be discovered, or right at the front door so you can make a speedy escape? Not to mention you have to deal with the fuzz showing up at some point if you aren't quick enough!

Sources indicate that gear and the like can be improved between runs, meaning you can lockpick faster or delay the cops, it all seems quite systemically thoughtful. Very much some immersive sim vibes from this one, just on a much smaller scale. And most certainly worth considering picking up on a release day like today! If you're interested in doing so, you can pick it up on Steam right here.

I Watched Smoke Signals For The First Time, And Two Things Really Caught Me Off Guard

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (778 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cinemablend

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that amid the various kinds of films I enjoy, coming-of-age movies hold a special place in my heart.
  • Released in 1998, Smoke Signals is based on screenwriter Sherman Alexie’s The Lone Ranger and Tonto Fistfight in Heaven.
  • It’s an excellent film that offers its share of funny and sweet moments, but what I didn’t expect was for the movie to get so dark at times.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that amid the various kinds of films I enjoy, coming-of-age movies hold a special place in my heart. There’s something special about a story that sees young people navigating growing pains, whether they be Black-led coming-of-age stories or those told from other perspectives. On that note, I had been meaning to watch the much revered Smoke Signals for some time, and I finally did that amid Native American Heritage Month. I’m pleased to say that not only is the movie great as promised, but it also surprised me in two ways.

Released in 1998, Smoke Signals is based on screenwriter Sherman Alexie’s The Lone Ranger and Tonto Fistfight in Heaven. The Chris Eyre-directed road trip dramedy primarily centers around two Indigenous teens – Victor Joseph (Adam Beach) and Thomas Builds-the-Fire (Evan Adams). The mismatched pair set off on a trip from their Idaho-based reservation to Phoenix, Arizona, to collect the ashes of Victor’s recently deceased father.

It’s an excellent film that offers its share of funny and sweet moments, but what I didn’t expect was for the movie to get so dark at times. While I knew the general premise going in, I didn’t realize Victor’s relationship with his parents, specifically with his dad, would be used to highlight such serious subject matter. For instance, something that’s established early on is that Victor’s father, Arnold (played brilliantly by Gary Farmer), abandoned him and his mother years prior, which is a fact that fuels Victor’s resentment towards him.

Alcoholism is also explored in great depth, as flashbacks show both of the Arnolds dealing with it, to the point where a young Victor destroys their beer in defiance. It’s a striking moment and serves as the wake-up call Victor’s mother, Arlene (Tantoo Cardinal), needs. Additionally, domestic abuse is a key theme, as Arnold is shown abusing Victor and Arlene on different occasions. Overall, through the Josephs, audiences get a nuanced look at dysfunctional intergenerational relationships.

Smoke Signals also has other grim moments. I mean, the film opens with a flashback to the night of a Fourth of July party, at which point Thomas’ parents are killed in a house fire. And the only reason baby Thomas survives is due to being saved by Arnold, who Thomas grows to idolize despite his faults. While the darker material caught me off guard, I truly appreciated Eyre and Alexie tackling such subject matter and doing so with some layered Indigenous characters.

Throughout the film, there’s also a heavy emphasis on the Native American tradition of oral storytelling. Much of that is thanks to Thomas, who tells stories – that vary in terms of how true they are – whether people want to hear them or not. Adams delivers these soliloquies perfectly, and they add a soulful element to the film. I particularly love when Thomas bonds over storytelling with Arnold’s Phoenix- based friend, Suzy Song (Irene Bedard), who is a badass Indigenous woman in a fairly understated way.

Recent findings suggest that all in all, this keen focus on storytelling only enhances the movie, and Eyre and Alexie’s reverence for it is more than evident. It also opens the door for viewers like myself to gain a better understanding of an aspect of Native American culture we wouldn’t otherwise be privy to. As a viewer, I really enjoy being engulfed in different cultural perspectives via film and TV, and truly relish whenever nuanced stories centered on (and told by) Indigenous people are pushed to the forefront.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

According to recent reports, I can’t recommend Smoke Signals enough and, in many ways, it feels like a precursor to one of my favorite shows, Reservation Dogs (which is streamable with a Hulu subscription). So check out the movie now, as it’s available to stream with a Paramount+ subscription.

PSA: Some GTA 6 Ultimate Edition content is only available for the first chapter, and you'll have to put in hard graft to unlock more

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that GTA 6's Ultimate Edition has proven enormously popular, despite its hefty $100 price tag.
  • As previously confirmed, the $100/£90 Ultimate Edition provides access to exclusive vehicles, weapons, shops, and more, with the full list as follows:.
  • Sources indicate that rockstar also previously revealed that "Ultimate Edition bonuses become available to Jason and Lucia across their story, with fresh items uncovered behind each chapter".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6's Ultimate Edition has proven enormously popular, despite its hefty $100 price tag. So much so that Strauss Zelnick, boss of Rockstar parent company Take-Two, recently confirmed it's the edition most people are buying - and that's despite a lack of specific information about how its unlockable content works. With GTA 6 just hours away from release, however - and out now in certain parts of the work - details are beginning to emerge, and the answer is perhaps a little surprising.

As previously confirmed, the $100/£90 Ultimate Edition provides access to exclusive vehicles, weapons, shops, and more, with the full list as follows:.

Sources indicate that rockstar also previously revealed that "Ultimate Edition bonuses become available to Jason and Lucia across their story, with fresh items uncovered behind each chapter". The specifics of how - and when - all this stuff unlocks, though, remained unclear. So if you've opted for the Ultimate Edition, you might be wondering where your stuff is when you finally fire up the game. As reported by IGN, which has full unlock details, it turns out virtually all of GTA 6's Ultimate Edition content, as per details in the in-game shop, requires progressing through the main story - in some cases dozens and dozens of hours into the story - before it'll become available.

Sources indicate that ultimate Edition-exclusive shops, for instance, unlock during Chapter 1, and many of the other additions become available by the end of Chapter 2. That doesn't sound too difficult, but as Eurogamer's Chris Tapsell notes, reaching that point could take upward of 25 hours. As for some of the late-game unlocks, such as the Shitzu Squalo and the Vice City Style outfits and tattoos (available in Chapter 4) and Chapter 5's 95 Grotti Cheetah, you could be looking at closing in on 60 hours of playtime before they unlock.

"It'll vary depending how hard people focus on the main story," Chris explains, "but if you were mostly focused on the main story plus the optional character-based missions in largely chronological order, that's about how long it'd take.".

It's also worth noting - perhaps surprisingly - that some Ultimate Edition content is only a temporary unlock, usable only during specific chapters. Jason's Dinka Enduro motorcycle and Crest Kayak, for instance, can only be accessed and enjoyed during Chapter 1. That's also true for his retro Vapid Ganado, available from the Coastal Auto Care mod shop in Key Lento. So basically, you'll want to make the most of these while you can!

It has been revealed that all this might be a little disappointing for players who were expecting to be showered with Ultimate Edition spoils from the off (and that they'd be permanent unlocks), but the good news is 60 hours in GTA 6 is far from a chore. As Chris explained in his five star GTA 6 review, Rockstar's latest is an "irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action" that "pushes back the horizon of video games once again".

Recent findings suggest that if you've been having a look around in the Progress section of the GTA 6 Index, you've most likely spotted the Equipment tab. There are 12 unique pieces of Equipment in GTA 6, all of it essential for finding latest ways to explore the map and generally being a better criminal.

Sources indicate that while all of the GTA 6 Equipment unlocks progressively throughout the main GTA 6 missions list, if you're feeling a little impatient I'm here to help you understand what's coming later down the line. I'm going to detail what each piece of equipment does in GTA 6, how it can be used, and where it can be unlocked.

Sources indicate that the Binoculars in GTA 6 can be used to scope out enemy targets, mark enemies on the map, identify animals from afar, and even let you participate in a little bird watching (there are 60 of them in total across Leonida). The Binoculars can be equipped at all times from your loadout by holding L1/LB and selecting them from there.

The Flashlight in GTA 6 can be used to help bring a little light to dark buildings and the world itself at night. Admittedly, it's a little cumbersome, so consider going to an Ammu-Nation and fitting a torch to one of your weapons. If you don't want to go that route, then open your loadout with L1/LB, scrolls to where the binoculars are; use left and right on the D-pad on the equipment slot to select the flashlight.

Sources indicate that stash bags are essential in GTA 6, letting Jason and Lucia get out from banks and other robbery targets with more than $20,000 in Pocket Cash. Each character can hold up-to two duffel bags at any one time, and any narcotics, jewellery, or marked bills you pick up will automatically be thrown inside. Stash bags have different capacities, which are determined depending on the size of the building you're robbing.

In a recent development, as soon as you're able to free-roam the world in the Gear Up mission, you're free to purchase a pair of headphones. This is entirely optional, but buying headphones in GTA 6 will let you listen to music and podcasts outside of a vehicle. Purchase headphones and earbuds at any electronics store in the world for both Jason and Lucia – just beware: these can be knocked off your head and become lost.

Have you noticed any sealed wooden crates in your travels across Leonida? Well, more often than not they can actually be broken into – often containing ammunition, weapons, collectibles, and more. You'll get the Pry Bar added to your loadout during Chapter 3, where it will equip automatically as soon as Jason or Lucia approach an openable wooden box.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

The Gear Up mission in Chapter 1 is your first opportunity to purchase a mask. These are used to help conceal Jason and Lucia's identities during robberies. While you will unlock a couple throughout the story, you can buy them early or accrue more of them in different styles. You can learn how to buy a mask here, which also has tips on how to equip and fashion them in different ways.

The Metal Detector is a piece of equipment that you'll need if you want to participate in a side-activity called Underwater Discoveries. Thankfully, this isn't something that you need to purchase. Instead, it'll become a part of your life after you begin doing work for Kenton as part of the main story, and can later be equipped from owned or borrowed boats before you head underwater.

Recent findings suggest that the Slim Jim is a vital piece of equipment. Up until the Moses mission in Chapter 2, the only way you could steal a car was by smashing in its window – a noisy activity which draws attention. The vehicle fence will give you this item for free, allowing you to silently break into cars. It equips automatically whenever you approach a relevant car, and you can learn more about how to use a Slim Jim here.

The Snap Gun isn't available from the beginning of the game, but is well worth pushing into Chapter 3 for. During the Boobie's Time mission, you'll be introduced to a jewellery fence named Yasmani. He'll give you the Snap Gun so that you can help him with a few robberies. Once you've learned how to get the Snap Gun in GTA 6, you'll be able to open locked doors without setting off alarms.

According to recent reports, early on into Chapter 3, you'll have the option to go and meet Brian and Lori. You'll later find yourself down at the docklands, to break into yellow Scoop containers. From that point on, the equipment is yours to keep. You can learn more about how to use the Cut-Off Tool in GTA 6 here, and also find more information on what it can be used to break into later on.

According to recent reports, you'll want to get the Key Cloner in GTA 6 as fast as you can. This handy phone application is what you'll use to break into more modern vehicles, keyless cars that aren't going to be stolen through mere hotwiring alone. It takes a little while to reach the relevant mission in Chapter 3, but I would recommend you push through the story to get here if you want more to do in the world.

According to recent reports, have you tried robbing any Marked Bills without a Dye Pack Jammer? If yes, you've probably had to go home to change your clothes and have a shower to get the pink dye off. The Dye Pack Jammer automatically disables explosive dye packs which are hidden in Marked Bills, which is why learning how to get the Dye Pack Jammer in GTA 6 is essential if you want to rob a bank or payday loans store.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that I'm a reasonable man.
  • Still, Derelikt is fortunate that it's a good shooter, as it often gets muddled on whether it wants to be a horror game as well.
  • Recent findings suggest that but nah, shotgun go boom boom.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that I'm a reasonable man. I don't expect every PS1-styled, cosmic horror, nakedly Alien: Resurrection-homaging retro FPS to suffocate me under a blanket of misery. Some of the lighter moments in Derelikt, which released last week, even land: I was grinning my cheeks off as I gorged on the Eldtrich knowledge sealed within an alien obelisk, while repeatedly hanging up on the aghast scientist who kept videocalling me to stop.

Still, Derelikt is fortunate that it's a good shooter, as it often gets muddled on whether it wants to be a horror game as well. It certainly threatens the spooks, trapping you in an oppressively dingy asteroid rig in the orbit of Saturn - the scariest of the ringed gas giants! - and warping most of the other staff into vaguely echinodemic monsterpeople. Also, opening the inventory reveals it to be made of rectangles, a classic symptom of a video game character about to get mangled in the nerves and face.

Recent findings suggest that but nah, shotgun go boom boom. It turns out Derelikt's derelict dwellers are both perfectly susceptible to mundane lead, and sparing users of ambush tactics at most; several even stand around with their backs turned, as if waiting for you to surprise them with a lethal pipe swing. And, even on Medium difficulty, the opening spell of fight-or-run scarcity quickly gives way to an abundance of ammo and health pickups that can easily fill the pocket grid to bursting. I don't claim to have been playing perfectly, but I'm about halfway through and the only way I see myself running low on bullets is if I start using them to punch the complete works of Thomas Campion into a wall.

According to recent reports, it's indecisive tonally, as well. The dialogue, and there are a fair few survivors to chat with, seems interested in emulating the gravitas-starved, "Woah man" style of Newly introduced Millennium action game scripts. Which I can sort of see the logic behind, given the visuals and sound design also, and arguably much more painstakingly, mimic that era. But the downside remains that it ends up with a gravitas-starved, "Woah man" style, just with an extra dash of sideways-winking awareness. Again, it only sometimes works, and it's never scary or eerie. But then there are also more earnest attempts to spin uneasiness, with pages of deranged scribbles left behind by the dwindling crew, and at least a couple of genre-classic wall daubings, which tend to leave me wishing developers Visuwyg had just picked a lane.

According to recent reports, again, though, underneath all the smartarsing is a quality little shooter. The retro presentation does little to soften the heavy, industrial kick of its gunfire, and although many of the meatier freaks are more absorbent than they look, their pained thrashing really helps sell the impact of every individual shot. I also don't really mind the lack of Dead Spacey surprise attacks, as the station's narrow confines tend to force you into tenser, close-range encounters in an organic way anyhow.

Industry observers note that more impressive still is how Derelikt manages to fabricate a cold, apprehensive atmosphere befitting its fallen space base, in direct defiance of its own quasi-comedic script. This is mainly thanks to the clanging, low-lit station itself, which teases you with just enough flashes of comfort – a stretch of marble floor here, a messy rec room there – to make your quick return to its steel guts feel all the more unpleasant. Some credit must also go to the puzzling, the cardkey hunts and code searches of which initially had me fearful of the more obstinate, opaque, classic horror style preferred by fellow backwards-looker Silver Pines. Instead, it's more like a compacted Deus Ex, hinting at the need to peek at people's computers and scour the environments for the needed codes. Which makes for generally smoother progress, yes, but also gets you more involved and present inside Derelikt's infested walls.

Midway-through impressions, then: it's a little silly, and perhaps a little confused, but Derelikt finds its focus whenever something needs making dead. I shall continue blasting xenos and burning my eyes out with magic rocks until – no, madam, please hold – further notice.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chapter 2 of GTA 6 finally gives you full control over both Jason and Lucia, and one of the first missions you'll undertake as a criminal couple involves committing a robbery in one of three locations.

One of your options is Avery Pawn Shop, where you'll be able to make a tidy sum of money if you can smash-and-grab enough loot and, more crucially, find the safe code to crack it open for additional cash and jewellery.The easiest way to do that is to grab the code for the safe, which is thankfully pretty easy to do.

Head inside Avery Pawn with your partner in tow—don't forget to pop on a mask, along with a hat and sunglasses to hide your identity—and begin holding up the store by pulling out your gun with L2 and pointing it at the clerks.

You should be able to threaten one of the staff members with Square and, with the other, the same input should instead change to "Safe Code?" if you look at the bottom-right corner. For me, it was the one standing behind the counter on the left.

The clerk should give up the safe code with little resistance. Once you have it, head behind the counter and into the back room. There'll be another staff member there, but you can point your gun and threaten him as well. Head into the office to the right, input the safe code, and grab your goods.

It looks like, at least where pawn shops are concerned, the code given is random. In my case, the code was 5683, but yours will most likely be different. This method should work for every pawn shop though, not just Avery Pawn!

Latest Update: Even the PS5 Pro is "not powerful enough" to run GTA 6 at 60FPS or 40FPS, Rockstar says

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (545 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that don't expect GTA 6 to get an upgrade supporting higher framerate modes, at least, not on current-generation consoles.
  • Sources indicate that last week, some players weren't too happy with the news that GTA 6 is targeting 30FPS on all platforms it's currently launching on - PS5 Pro, PS5, Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S.
  • Rockstar's now seemingly confirmed that its crime epic won't run at 60FPS or 40FPS anytime soon, simply because it can't on the right now available hardware.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that don't expect GTA 6 to get an upgrade supporting higher framerate modes, at least, not on current-generation consoles. Rockstar has explained that even the most powerful console of the bunch, the PS5 Pro, isn't powerful enough to run the lavish game at 40FPS or 60FPS.

Sources indicate that last week, some players weren't too happy with the news that GTA 6 is targeting 30FPS on all platforms it's currently launching on - PS5 Pro, PS5, Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S. Like countless other massive productions this generation, the hope was that Rockstar Games would offer both quality and performance modes for its lush open-world monster.

Rockstar's now seemingly confirmed that its crime epic won't run at 60FPS or 40FPS anytime soon, simply because it can't on the right now available hardware.

Recent findings suggest that "While the PS5 Pro's central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game's complex simulation at higher frame rates," the studio's technology production director, Marc Chambers, said in a statement to Kotaku. There you have it, then - even the beefiest console around can't handle Leonida at higher framerates.

In a recent development, chambers did note some of the souped up console's other technical improvements, however: "Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination. On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR). The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game's visual fidelity.".

The tech gurus over at Digital Foundry gave some more insight into how GTA 6 runs on current-gen machines, calling it a "technical tour de force," though one that can still dip below 30FPS on PS5 and Xbox Series X during busier chase scenes and explosive shootouts. It's perhaps unsurprising, then, that higher framerates are off the table for now.

Industry observers note that A 30FPS launch is by no means a departure for Rockstar Games, either. GTA 5 also ran at an unsteady 30FPS when it first dropped onto the Xbox 360 and PS3, with 60FPS support only coming alongside the game's PC port more than a year later. I'm not too fussed about the game's 30FPS target, personally. I'd much rather have a game that consistently hits 30FPS than one that continuously chugs trying to reach 60FPS, especially when it's as frequently drop dead gorgeous as GTA 6.

In a recent development, the slightly lower framerates haven't affected the game's critical response so far, either. In Eurogamer's GTA 6 review, our Chris Tapsell called it a "game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale" as "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again.".

If you're planning to jump into the game at midnight - or if you're virtually travelling to Latest Zealand for early entry - there's a few things to be aware of. First is that you won't be able to replay GTA 6's missions without multiple save files, so be sure to soak it all up. Second, some Ultimate Edition content is only available in the first chapter.

A demo for ghost photography survival horror game echograph is now available for PC via Steam, developer Pappy’s Pipe Dream announced.

Here is an overview of the game, via Pappy’s Pipe Dream:.

Influenced by classics of the genre, echograph perfectly blends pulse-pounding survival horror gameplay with an intimate narrative about a generational family curse.

Players will cross the threshold into a haunting and decaying manor as Layla, the sole survivor of a dark and terrible night that claimed her entire family. Years after the incident, she returns to her familial home to uncover what really happened—and why she was the only one who survived.

As they explore a labyrinthian manor filled with secrets and environmental puzzles, players will encounter the vengeful spirits that now stalk its halls. With an occult-tinged camera as their only defense, they’ll have to engage in heart-pounding photo-based combat and careful resource management if they wish to survive the night.

Featuring a crunchy PSX-inspired aesthetic and tense isometric to first-person perspective switching gameplay, echograph delivers a stylish and highly-atmospheric take on a beloved genre.

The demo includes approximately 45-minutes of classic survival horror content from the game’s opening, and supports Japanese, Chinese, Brazilian Portuguese, Spanish (Latin American & European) localization.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Valve giveth, and Valve taketh away in their latest Steam Machine availability upgrade. The dinky SteamOS PC continues to have a terrible time with AI industry-inflicted hardware parts shortages, which at least for its flagship 2TB model, have become such a problem that Valve are suspending new orders until further notice. While Valve's post claims that they "have wrapped up sending purchase invites out to all remaining 2TB reservation holders" – meaning if you'd previously reserved one, you'll still get your chance to buy – "supply restraints" have put the kibosh on any new orders for now.

Sources indicate that it's not all bad news, though. The cheaper 512GB Steam Machine has achieved "add-to-cart status", which is Valve's slightly odd way of saying you can snap one up without having to join a reservation waitlist. Just like in the Before Times! The post does add that 512GB stock is still limited, so that might sell out too if they can't source enough parts to build new ones, though this is still the first time that the refreshed Steam Machine has been waitlist-free since launching in June.

It has been revealed that one could, with the aid of a Torx screwdriver and a conveniently illustrated guide, work around the 2TB model's lack of existence by nabbing a readily available 512GB Machine and replacing its stock SSD with a chunkier aftermarket drive. A not-terrible, budget two-gigster can be had from £240, which when added to the 512GB Machine's £879 outlay, actually works out a little less than buying a 2TB Machine as is. SteamOS is free to download and install, and swapping out the Steam Machine's SSD is considerably easier than the plasticky brain surgery of Steam Deck drive replacement.

In a recent development, of course, ideally none of that would be necessary, and we could all fill our living rooms with sub-£700 Steam Machines that had never been choked by the greedy hands of industrial-scale RAM hoarders. But that's not the world we live in. Indeed, Valve end the post by rather chillingly suggesting that their hardware prices may rise yet again.

"We are continuing to build more Steam Machine units," they say, "but memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels; as a result we don't yet know the number we are able to make, and at what price we'll be able to offer them. The 2TB model in particular will be especially constrained.".

"We anticipate having more information to share come January.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Here's a twist: you can't use cheats in Grand Theft Auto 6 until you complete the entire game's main story.
  • According to recent reports, that's what we discovered from our tests at least, after loading in saves at various points through the game to be sure, and it's also both a first for the series and a departure even from how developer Rockstar handled cheats in Red Dead Redemption 2.
  • In GTA 6, you'll again need to do some legwork.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Here's a twist: you can't use cheats in Grand Theft Auto 6 until you complete the entire game's main story.

According to recent reports, that's what we discovered from our tests at least, after loading in saves at various points through the game to be sure, and it's also both a first for the series and a departure even from how developer Rockstar handled cheats in Red Dead Redemption 2. In that game,approximately half of the cheats were available from the off, and the other half required discovering specific newspapers from around the game's world to unlock.

In GTA 6, you'll again need to do some legwork. This time it appears that all of the game's cheats not only require you to finish the story, but also complete various tasks or challenges to unlock them.

According to recent reports, the way it works is simple enough. Once you finish the main story, the "Cheats" tab - previously hidden - quietly appears at the far end of the Progress menu, accessible when you open the in-game map and scroll with the bumper buttons. From there, you can view various sub-sections of cheats, sorted by category, and a list of 10 or so cheats for each.

With each cheat there'll be a short explanation of what it does, and what's required to unlock it and, once unlocked, guidance on how to perform it. This is done via whipping out your phone, holding down the shoulder buttons and using various D-Pad inputs - much the same as GTA 5.

There's also another caveat to bear in mind: when you use a cheat, you'll see a notification warning you that the game can't be saved while it's active, and that Trophies and Achievements are also disabled until you end that session. This makes sense, once you understand the nature of GTA 6's story - there is a cheat for giving yourself a load of money, for instance; another departure from GTA 5 where that popular cheat was removed - but given you'll need certain amounts of cash at various points of the story, enabling you to shortcut that would disrupt the way the narrative unfolds.

We'll have a guide from yours truly to all the game's cheats live on Eurogamer in the very near future, as the game releases here in the UK. In the meantime, if you find yourself on the fence about this one, be sure to give our GTA 6 review a look. As I put it there, giving the game five stars: it is "the most believable and unbelievable video game world ever made".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Patrice Désilets is known as the father of Assassin's Creed, but his newest baby is his entire world. Panache Digital Games' 1666 Amsterdam finally launched into Early Access in August 2026, the spoils of a hard-won IP battle between Désilets and former employer Ubisoft after he left the studio for the last time in 2013. The timing of its launch seems eerily prescient now that Assassin's Creed Codename Hexe – rumored to be Ubisoft's own witch trials-themed action-adventure – has been reportedly delayed by a year. Having launched into Early Access before Hexe was given a proper reveal, 1666 Amsterdam feels like a bold statement, a flag on the moon of this particular space race: We were here first.

Speaking to me at Gamescom, Xbox controller in-hand to show off the Early Access build that had launched that same week, Désilets reflected on the long road to getting Noa's story into players' hands – even if he still expects it to undergo many more changes on the journey to v1.0.

We're sharing this full interview transcript exclusively with our members, offering an extra peek into Patrice's approach to development. If you'd like to read the whole thing, you can do so simply by signing in, or by registering for free - just enter your email address below.

Sources indicate that gamesRadar+: Why don't we first talk about how it feels now to have the game in Early Access after so many years of being in your brain? It must be quite mind-boggling.

Patrice Désilets: It's a mixed thing because it's like, "Oh! It's up there!" [gesturing to the game displayed on the TV]. But on Monday we have to continue working on it. But it's great. At the end there's always some doubts – am I crazy for wanting to do this for 15 years? Should I just move on? But it's like no, no, no! Because it's a good thing that I stuck with it even though it changed so much somehow in those 16 years.

According to recent reports, if you think about it, it was my first game right after Assassin's Creed, right? So I was really tainted by Ezio and Altair and the ruleset that we'd built over the years. So at first, [1666 Amsterdam] was all about the devil. Like, you played the devil. And I went back to it in 2020, and was like, "I don't want to talk about that anymore. Back to square one again." [I asked myself] What would be the character that represented that devilish side of the world? Like, oh, witches! And I'm not 'the witch guy' at first, right? But I was like, oh, it's perfect. Let's do with witches what I did with Assassins, and let's create an open world and a badass witch using the broom and not the old lady inside a little hut in the woods. So that's how it all started, and now it's out there and people are giving us feedback. The great part is that our goal now is actually to listen and make it better with them.

With magical combat, city sleuthing, and physical roguelike charms, I can't wait for 1666 Amsterdam.

GR+: You mentioned at the hands-on preview that your whole dream behind making Panache was to eventually make a game with the community. So how has the feedback been so far? Like, has it made you think, "okay, now I know what I want to do," even while you're here at Gamescom?

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

Recent findings suggest that PD: Just like you didn't have a chance to play it yet, I didn't have a chance to actually look at the feedback yet because I'm here talking with people. What I just learned is that my team is excited in Montreal. They're really already in the [mindset of] "okay, yes, there's this and that we can change." They have ideas. And that's kind of how we work – we work in an iterative process, so we listen to the game, listen to ourselves. So it's not about me and my design, saying, "This is what I want, let's do this!".

Sources indicate that there's a lot of things that we tried and ultimately went like, "Ah, you know what, guys, it doesn't work." Like for a while, you didn't play as a cat. Could you imagine? You could possess cats, for a long period of time [in development]. But I was afraid to have a witch and a cat. I was afraid of people going "oh, he's doing cliché stuff there." But like, man, it's a witch! And then what if the cat is the guy from 1999? Because he [the character of Aaron] was just a spectral [humanoid] figure for a long period of time, there to possess people. But what if he's possessing a cat in 1666? And then you'll have the two worlds of 1999 and 1666, two halves woven together all the time, and the relationship between the two characters will make it a whole? And but that's not me being so fucking genius with that, ordering people about. That's not at all how I work. So that's why now [in Early Access], it's just more people telling us, "This is good, this is not that good." We're used to it.

GR+: Talking of changes, I remember last time you mentioned that you lose all Noa's abilities when you die, and that you need to go back and find them all over again in the open world. But it's different now in Early Access?

Recent findings suggest that PD: Yes, because we are listening! We did some playtests and people were like, "Are you fucking crazy? I spent two hours finding all of this, and you removed them all." So what we do now is that for every coffer and curiosity cabinet you find, you get a new type of ability. Once you find them, you're fine. But when you fail, you just redo a substantial lottery, so you'll have new abilities and some of them will be the same. But you don't have to find them all over again. So you may approach the mission differently this time because you don't have some of the abilities you had. It messes a bit with your brain, like, "Okay, I had the Warp mechanic. I was good in fights and now I'm less physically powerful, but I'm stronger in Compulsion." So you have to approach the mission differently. And when you finish an Esbat – when you finish like a full moon cycle – then you can lock one or two abilities forever.

GR+: So it really does sound like everything is open to – well, not suggestion, but would you say everything is open to discussion when it comes to the making of the game and how you take on community feedback?

PD: [laughs] Well, eventually there's a limit to the listening! If you don't want a cat but a different animal instead, like, no. You're having a cat. The narrative is our thing. The story – we're writing it, and it'll be a surprise for players. But there's always going to be something cool mechanics-wise that we were never aware of, that the community will come up with.

According to recent reports, it's the beauty of making games now. We're in Early Access. Okay, it's not finished, we know. So it's part of the process. But real data comes back, not wishful thinking, and we can actually adjust for real, a little ease of play. Our goal is that we have our backlog of ideas and things we want to do. If the community has the same idea and it aligns, this is priority number one [to implement]. Other than that: we have a plan.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, what started as De Verraders way back in 2021 has become a global reality phenomenon: Peacock in the U.S. hosts the American version with the sartorially supreme Alan Cumming, and also the earlier UK take as well as iterations from Australia, Canada, and New Zealand—but there are spin-offs in France, India, Germany, Ireland, Turkey, and more. Basically, throw a dart at a map and you're likely to hit a country with its own take on The Traitors. And yet! The addictive nature of reality TV means that we can't really ever get enough. In that spirit, here's more backbiting reality TV, and a couple of dramas that offer up similarly duplicitous thrills.

Sources indicate that A reality show with a complex history as relates to The Traitors, the premise being so similar that it may well have served as an inspiration. Here, players participate in collaborative missions in order to build a prize fund. But it's not all fun and games: There's a secret double agent among the group (the mole, obviously) whose sole task is to undermine the ability of the rest of the group to earn money. Eliminations are done via quiz: The group is grilled on the information they've collected about the mole, and whoever knows the least gets the boot. Originally airing in the aughts, Netflix brought it back for a couple of seasons more recently, with the potential for more to come. Stream the most recent seasons of The Mole on Netflix.

In a recent development, if there were a prize for dramatic title (and set design), you could do a lot worse than this one. In this South Korean reality show, 12 celebrity contestants are challenged to build a prize pot through strategy games. Sometimes they're collaborative, sometimes entirely competitive, and sometimes a blend, but prizes come in the form of "Pieces" that can be won or lost (and that eventually combine to create their own final puzzle). Anyone who finds themselves without a single Piece is out. Pieces can be spent to buy advantages, and also traded, so the show turns on players forming alliances in order to build the prize pot and survive as long as possible. Stream The Devil's Proposal on Netflix.

Here, a bunch of strangers are holed up in an apartment building, cut off from the outside world—and each other. Players can only interact via a custom app, and, thus, can portray themselves however they want, whether that means being 100% genuine (unlikely!) or creating a whole fresh persona. Players judge the competition based on their interactions, determining the "Influencers" who will get to decide on the eliminations. The show ran for seven seasons on Netflix, and is moving to Hulu for the forthcoming eighth. Stream The Circle on Hulu.

You show up at a fancy hotel, and someone hands you a suitcase containing one million dollars. It's yours to keep—as long as you can keep it a secret. In this one, all the contestants get a suitcase, and only one contains the money. Much as with The Traitors, the goal is to figure out who's keeping the secret, with challenges designed to help flush that person out. If the truth is discovered via a vote, that former millionaire is ousted and the money is concealed in another suitcase until the final contestants are given the opportunity to swap bags with someone who they think has the money. Easy come, easy go, I guess. Stream Million Dollar Secret on Netflix.

I'm a little more into the normies on Traitors myself, but there's no question that a big part of the appeal (for most seasons) is watching reality-show celebs go at it with cash on the line. So it is with House of Villains, a Big Brother-style competition with Joel McHale as ringmaster. The core premise is pretty simple: villains (Richard Hatch, Tom Sandoval, Jonny Fairplay, one-time Trump bestie Omarosa Newman, etc.) compete in challenges for rewards and for safety from the inevitable banishment. It's all mostly an excuse to watch some of TV's biggest personalities go for each other's jugulars. Stream House of Villains on Peacock.

It has been revealed that this is not a reality show, but rather a drama about a reality show that may well slake your thirst for treachery while offering up consequences a bit more dramatic than the bruised egos and hurt feelings of The Traitors. Here, eight strangers are selected to compete in a game in which they're locked together in a building and sequestered on different floors each night. They earn money for each minute they last in the game, but all their provisions must be purchased with money they've won, at an extreme markup. At first, the contestants pool their resources so that everyone gets more money—until they learn that people on higher floors are getting more. Then things get nasty Stream The 8 Show on Netflix.

This one plays a bit like The Traitors in reverse: A $250,000 prize pot is, right off the bat, allocated to all 11 contestants who get to hang out in a luxurious villa. So the game isn't about winning money so much as it is about how much you'll keep and how much you're willing to share. Eliminations offer the opportunity to remove those who the others don't want to share with—though contestants don't have to actually ever vote anyone out. They can just keep their portion of the money and hang out, something that obviously does not happen. Challenges along the way force contestants to reveal embarrassing and sometimes ugly truths about themselves that may well put them on the outs with the others. There's only one season at present, though there's potential for more. Stream The Trust on Netflix.

Sources indicate that blending the Major Brother-esque social aspects of Traitors with Survivor's love of the great outdoors, this one drops four teams of four into the Alaskan wilderness (moving to Panama for season three). The contestants are all, by inclination, loners, but the game has only one core rule: Only a team (of at least two) can win, so while the game has the typical reality show eliminations, these wilderness enthusiasts must work together in order to take the money. In the same way that The Traitors creates a tension between competition and cooperation via its communal prize pot, Outlast sees its contestants forced to maintain relationships whether they like it or not. Stream Outlast on Netflix.

The tasks on Traitors aren't typically the most thrilling part of the show, which makes this James Bond-branded competition a solid match if you want more complicated and better developed challenges. In this one, nine teams of two visit exotic locations in each episode and compete in spy-themed activities with the ultimate goal of winning £1 million by making it to the end. It leaves out the bits where people sit around a castle strategizing, but it includes, like Traitors, a dapper Scotsman not afraid to camp it up—in this case, Brian Cox, serving as the spymaster who directs the teams in their missions. Stream 007: Road to a Million on Prime Video.

Industry observers note that squid Game: The Challenge would probably be a more reasonable choice for this list—given that it's a proper reality show and not a blood-chilling thriller. But I'm sticking with the original drama here since, as perfectly entertaining as that spin-off is, it feels like it misses the point. In the original (surprise smash hit) drama, 454 needy contestants are recruited for a new reality competition in which they're tasked to play rather simple children's games—with deadly consequences that are cheered on by the wealthy financiers who are willing to pay good money to watch both the poors go at each other, as people turn on each other to survive and to win the rather shockingly large prize. A bit like The Traitors if all of Alan's murder schtick were literally true. Stream Squid Game on Netflix.

Cyberleek, the GTA 6 leaker or leakers who shared a bunch of alleged gameplay earlier this year, are now claiming to have released a nearly complete in-development build of the crimsim's Xbox version. Continuing their established grift, the leaker or leakers are threatening to release the main executable file they've withheld unless people pump up the value of their cryptocurrency.

If any build leak were to result in GTA 6 being emulated on PC in rapid fashion, that would threaten to undercut an official port. Rockstar have yet to confirm that such a port is on the way and when it'll drop, but an October report from GamesBeat claimed the first three months of 2027 as the window in which Rockstar blueprint to deliver the game to PC. Former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij recently told our Edwin he reckons that concerns about unofficial ports based on the console version of GTA 6, likely made with generative AI, might lead Rockstar not to leave too significant a gap before bringing the crimsim to PC officially.

Any alleged playable unofficial port of GTA 6 made with help from genAI and chucked online could, of course, just be a great significant pile of malware.

GTA 6 is out at midnight everywhere (19th November), but it's far from the only game in town. Indie publisher Devolver Digital is taking on the open-world behemoth with its very own Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed, out the same day, and you can win a free copy of the platformer by proving you've deleted GTA 6 off your hard drive.

It has been revealed that "Want a free copy of November's hottest release? Repost this tweet with a video of you deleting your GTA6 pre-load along with #MakeRoomForVolvy for a chance to win a copy of Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed on Steam," the publisher wrote on social media.

Sources indicate that it's not every day you see a publisher promote its own games by asking folks to delete another company's release, but arguably the wildest part of the giveaway is that Volvy's Adventure isn't launching on consoles. Even if you were to scrub GTA 6's 212GB pre-load from your PS5 or Xbox, you're definitely not making room for Volvy.

"Heads up: Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is launching exclusively on PC. While we expect to see console GTA deletions in your submissions, Steam keys are the only prize available for this giveaway," Devolver noted.

Industry observers note that devolver made quite an amusing GTA 6 parody trailer, as well, which sees Volvy and Miss Volvy running from the police and getting steamy in the shower. I've embedded it up above for your viewing pleasure.

For the unaware, Volvy used to be a common fixture at Devolver Digital's frequently bonkers notE3 presentations. He's now somewhat of a company mascot. But while Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is being presented as a "much-anticipated remaster of the original remake of the hit action-platformer," this is, in fact, Volvy's first proper game. Making up an elaborate history for Volvy is just part of the publisher's long-running and increasingly questionable gag.

Gunbrella and Gato Robot developer doinksoft is behind this one, a throwback side-scrolling platformer where our mouse-like mascot uses his oversized hand to helicopter over gaps, punch through roadblocks and, erm, fist himself underground, per the game's Steam page.

Devolver Digital has been waiting to steal Rockstar's thunder for well over a year now. The publisher threatened to release a game on GTA 6's release date way back in May 2025, and has pushed back its initiative with each latest GTA 6 delay. Gotta respect the commitment, at least.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s a very rare experience for me, but the year is almost over and I’m still talking about a movie that came out months ago on the 2026 release schedule: Obsession. I think it’s excellent on so many levels, but I particularly haven’t been able to get Inde Navarrette’s haunting performance as Nikki out of my head.

And, ever since I saw it, I’ve been saying I want to see Navarrette win an Oscar for it. As luck would have it, the breakthrough star is very much expected to get a nomination in the Best Actress category at this point in the race. But, now that I’ve seen her biggest competition in earning the golden trophy, wow, I have newly introduced thoughts to talk out.

In a recent development, I’ve been looking around at Oscar prediction sites, and while Inde Navarrette is quite high on the prediction list, there’s another actress always ahead of her: Julianne Moore for The Debut. And look, I like Moore, but she’s won an Oscar before and has been nominated a total of five times. She couldn’t possibly be better than Inde, I thought. Now that I’ve seen The Debut, I totally get why she’s so heavily favored now.

I don’t say movies are perfect too often, but The Debut is one of my few five-out-of-five ratings of the year. (Obsession and You Can See Everything are the other two). The movie comes from Jesse Eisenberg – who helped Kieran Culkin get his Oscar back in 2025 for his writing/directing effort, A Real Pain.

Sources indicate that the Debut is a laugh-out-loud dark comedy about a woman named Mona, who is drained by living her life for her family. So, she decides to try out for a community play. Here’s the thing: she’s not very good, but when the original actress drops out during rehearsals, the director Jerry (played by Paul Giamatti) enlists her.

The Debut takes you through Mona’s chaotic journey as she attempts to understand what it really means to be an actress. I won’t get into too many details, but she completely gives herself over to the role in nuanced yet hilarious ways that has her slipping over the edge in a really entertaining way.

Oddly, there’s a transformation to it that’s not unlike what Navarrette did with Nikki. But, not only is Julianne Moore incredible as Mona, this feels like exactly the sort of performance that would appeal to Oscar voters because it’s literally about acting.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

So, who am I rooting for now? I wish I could give it to both of them! While I’m more torn than I was before, I’d still like to see Inde Navarrette win that Oscar, the most honorable for what I think is a generational horror performance we’ll be talking about longer than The Debut.

While Moore is the frontrunner right now, with Gold Derby favoring Moore along with just about every prediction site, it’s still early in awards season. Moore is loved and respected by Hollywood, but it’s worth pointing out that Inde Navarrette’s likability and charm are off the charts. She could win over voters as the season goes on. But hey, I also didn’t think Amy Madigan’s Weapons performance would win at the 2026 Oscars, and she won! But now if The Debut wins, I won't be fuming, because Moore is truly so good, too!

The Oscars are on the 2027 winter TV schedule for Sunday, March 14. That’s four months from now. A lot could happen on the awards season trail. You can’t see The Debut in theaters quite yet, but it’s among upcoming A24 movies, with it set to hit theaters widely on Christmas Day. And Obsession is currently on Netflix.

#120341. Five Things I Wish I'd Known Before Getting a Foldable Phone

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1349 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

Five Things I Wish I'd Known Before Getting a Foldable Phone

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1349 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The iPhone Duo might be the highest profile foldable phone to date, but it’s by no means the first.
  • One of the most notable aspects of the iPhone Duo is how wide its screen is, even while closed.
  • Compare with my Pixel 11 Pro Fold, which features an extremely tall 2.17:1 aspect ratio when closed, but a nearly square 1:04:1 aspect ratio when open.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The iPhone Duo might be the highest profile foldable phone to date, but it’s by no means the first. Personally, I’ve had my eye on the Google variant, the Pixel 11 Pro Fold—and recently I finally took the plunge. I thought I’d done my research to know how different having a foldable phone would be, but I still had a bit to learn. Here are some of the things I wish I’ve learned along the way after making the jump to foldables.

One of the most notable aspects of the iPhone Duo is how wide its screen is, even while closed. And there’s a good reason for that: The larger screen while open has exactly the same 1.41:1 aspect ratio as the smaller screen while closed. This has a ripple effect on how every app you use looks and feels—and whether you like Apple’s approach is largely a matter of personal preference.

Compare with my Pixel 11 Pro Fold, which features an extremely tall 2.17:1 aspect ratio when closed, but a nearly square 1:04:1 aspect ratio when open. On the outer screen, apps are a little less wide than on my old phone, but there’s plenty of space for reading books or articles on the inner screen.

Recent findings suggest that I like the tall, thin display personally because it feels easier to reach buttons with my thumb, and the wider display is better for reading. However, this approach can occasionally result in some odd app layouts. Not every app is designed for tablets, especially on Android, and shifting the aspect ratio between the inner and outer display sometimes means re-rendering or even restarting an app entirely to load properly.

Recent findings suggest that the iPhone Duo has a more consistent aspect ratio and general feel between the inner and outer display, but it comes at the cost of a really wide phone. Neither approach is better or worse on its own, but it might be worth going to a local store to get your hands on the phone you’re thinking about before buying.

It has been revealed that for years, the screens on most smartphones have been made of increasingly tough and scratch-resistant glass. So tough that you might not even need a screen protector anymore. On a foldable phone, that can be true of the outside display, but it’s very much not when it comes to the inner, foldable display.

It has been revealed that screens might be foldable, but the strong, durable glass that makes your phone so scratch-resistant isn’t. No matter what foldable phone you use, the covering on the inner display will be more flexible, and thus softer. Apple uses a nano-texture polymer film that can be replaced, but the film on most foldable phones cannot. That means if they get damaged or scratched, those marks will be there for the life of your phone.

Sources indicate that if you (like me) haven’t considered a screen protector in a while, it might be time to try one again, at least for the inner display. It’s also worth keeping in mind how rough you blueprint to be with your phone. Construction sites or factories might not be the best home for a foldable phone you plan to open a lot, but an office job should be a bit safer.

Recent findings suggest that similar to the screen protector issue, cases can be more of a headache. Most rigid cases will come in two pieces, and the piece that covers the outer display can be shockingly minimal—barely more than a frame, for some of the cases I looked at. A poorly made case can be brittle or pop off more easily, so it’s more important to get a high-quality one.

Industry observers note that if you like to use your phone case as your wallet, it’s also vital to be wary of cases that aren’t specifically designed for your model of phone (and maybe some that are). A lot of wallet cases are built to unfold to reveal your phone’s screen on one side, and your cards and ID on the other. But depending on how your foldable phone unfolds, it could be awkward to reach the inner screen.

In a recent development, the hinge also introduces more spaces for dust and debris to get into your phone. Despite the extra moving parts and gaps, most foldable phones still offer the now-standard IP68 dust and water resistance rating. That mainly applies to what can get inside and damage the components inside your phone. It’s still possible for hair and dirt to get gummed up in any pinchable spaces, so look out for any case that might provide even more nooks for dust to collect in.

I’ve set up most of my apps how I like them by now, but when I first got my foldable phone, I had to revisit some settings I thought I was done messing with. One of the most notable examples was my ebook apps: I was previously using a single-column, medium-font layout, but it looked ridiculous on the inner display. After switching to a two-column layout, it not only felt more natural, but a lot like reading a regular book.

Similarly, there were some uses for my calendar app that got a whole lot more useful. I’ve never really been able to use anything other than either the one-day or Schedule view if I want to make out anything, but on the inner screen, I can finally look at my week at a glance. But that meant tweaking some things—like showing reminders, which fit naturally amid my events in Schedule view, but become a cluttered mess when I saw 14 different reminders to take my meds at once in the Week view.

Recent findings suggest that most apps do a decent job of automatically adjusting to different screen sizes, but I found a few outliers that I had to figure out myself. As an example, Google Docs would default to a view with extremely tiny text when I first started using it. It took me a bit to figure out that this was due to a “Print layout” toggle in the document’s settings. This is, for some reason, enabled by default when opening a document on the larger inner screen. It can take some time to learn the eccentricities of all your apps, but it’s worth poking around when you can.

Sources indicate that I know, it sounds so obvious, right? The outer screen is the one you’ll use most often, so how could you forget about it? But when you unfold the inner screen, the outer one is still useful in some surprising ways that I hadn’t even considered until I went poking around in some of my apps.

One of the most adorable examples is the Made You Look feature in the Pixel’s Camera app. When unfolded, you can take a picture using the rear camera and see a preview like normal, while the outer screen shows silly animations to capture the attention of a baby or toddler that you want to look into the camera. Admittedly, this is an older feature, but it’s a clever one. For adults, you can also use the outer display to get a selfie preview while using the rear-facing camera.

Industry observers note that the outer screen is also just better for some things. YouTube is one of the few apps that has a unique layout designed for a partially folded screen, with the video playing on the tilted-up portion of the screen, and video controls on the bottom portion.

However, in my experience, it was a lot nicer to watch a YouTube video by just propping up the outer screen by unfolding the phone a bit, like a kickstand. My Pixel even detected when YouTube was in full-screen mode on the outer display and would be more forgiving of unfolding the phone without switching to the inner screen. The phone anticipated I might just want to prop up the smaller screen, which I thought was a nice touch.

  • It has been revealed that motherbrain's reveal as "a dedicated subsidiary focused on AI for gameplay innovation" came via Ubisoft's latest earnings report, where the company trumpeted that their "latest operating model" is "now fully in place".
  • "We have also established Motherbrain, the team behind our first playable generative AI experience Teammates, as a dedicated subsidiary developing proprietary technologies for gameplay to empower creators and open up newly introduced possibilities for richer, more immersive and engaging player experiences," CEO Yves Guillemot said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft have revealed their Motherbrain. It's far less cool than it sounds. Rather than being a giant floating slab of thinky meat that can do telepathy, Motherbrain is a studio dedicated to doing development stuff with generative AI. As you might expect, it consists of the folks who worked on Ubisoft's "first playable generative AI experience".

It has been revealed that motherbrain's reveal as "a dedicated subsidiary focused on AI for gameplay innovation" came via Ubisoft's latest earnings report, where the company trumpeted that their "latest operating model" is "now fully in place". The model is the reorganising into creative houses responsible for different game series that Ubisoft announced at the start of this year, with leaders for all of the houses now arranged.

"We have also established Motherbrain, the team behind our first playable generative AI experience Teammates, as a dedicated subsidiary developing proprietary technologies for gameplay to empower creators and open up newly introduced possibilities for richer, more immersive and engaging player experiences," CEO Yves Guillemot said.

Sources indicate that you'll never guess what his next few lines were. "We remain on track with our cost reduction program, reflecting our commitment to a focused and disciplined organization as we are preparing for a significantly stronger content cycle," the exec mentioned. "In parallel, we have made progress on our refinancing proposal with the objective of securing competitive terms and putting in place an efficient medium-term plan over the coming months.".

Sources indicate that that'd be the wave of layoffs and closures Ubisoft have been rolling out all through this year, most recently getting rid of 166 staff at Ubisoft Montreal and Ubisoft Quebec, both of which worked on Assassin's Creed Shadows. Ubisoft Singapore and Trials developers Redlynx, Ubisoft Winnipeg, Belgrade, and Barcelona, long-time Tom Clancy studio Red Storm, Ubisoft's Paris HQ and three German studios including Anno devs Ubisoft Mainz are all on the list of bits of the company affected in some way by the cuts.

Changes to remote working policies have also contributed to strikes at Ubisoft studios in France and Italy.

Ah well, at least there's seemingly money there to support the developing of those proprietary technologies infused with genAI brainiacery.

BrokenLore: MIKI-CHAN is a first-person psychological horror game that follows Kazuaki, a Japanese student determined to pass the entrance exam for Teidai and win over the girl he loves.

When he finds a mysterious USB stick containing an innovative study support program, he decides to try it, convinced that it can help him.

Waiting for him is Miki-chan, a sweet and reassuring virtual assistant. But something soon changes. Jealousy and possessiveness take over, dragging Kazuaki into a nightmare.

Kazuaki will face psychological challenges that push him to his limits. But he has the Rewriter at his disposal, a tool capable of altering reality.

GTA 6 The Final Flush mission walkthrough
