📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the Big Flush in GTA 6 is an optional mission, but it's well worth your time for a permanent stamina upgrade.
  • Industry observers note that to start The Final Flush mission in GTA 6, go to the bathroom block toward the north tip of Corsair Key in Mariana County (just north-east of Key Lento).
  • In a recent development, scan to learn the truth #NOFLUSHERS" with a QR code attached.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the Big Flush in GTA 6 is an optional mission, but it's well worth your time for a permanent stamina upgrade. You can start this GTA 6 mission from Chapter 1 onwards, and once it's done it's incredibly useful reward will allow you to do energy-draining activities, like running and swimming, for longer. It's also just a fun side mission to do. After finding an odd poster in a men's bathroom stall, you are enlisted to help oddball Dr. Merle to prove his bizarre conspiracy theory that the government is stealing DNA from poop (which is seemingly based on a real report about Putin) and things only get stranger from there.

Industry observers note that to start The Final Flush mission in GTA 6, go to the bathroom block toward the north tip of Corsair Key in Mariana County (just north-east of Key Lento). It should be easy to find as it's the only building in Corsair Key. Enter the men's toilet and you'll see a handmade poster on the wall that states "Stop! Don't Flush.

In a recent development, scan to learn the truth #NOFLUSHERS" with a QR code attached. Use your WaiNK IT app to scan the code and you'll receive a message from an Automated Machine that tells you to reply "TRUTH" to join the No Flushers movement. Select the "Truth" reply and you'll receive another message telling you that whoever is messaging will be at Frank's Waffles in Vice City. If asked, you need to repeat the code: 00-00-02.

Industry observers note that you need to meet the mystery No Flusher at Frank's Waffles in the Tequesta neighborhood of Vice City, in Vice-Dale County. When you enter the waffle house, you'll find a man muttering to himself in one of the booths nearest the toilets. However, he seemingly won't appear if it's not night time, as, when I went during the day, the mission icon had a padlock on it and the man wasn't there.

It has been revealed that when you get near the man, he covers up whatever he's working on and tells you that he's holding a royal flush. When he asks do you have a "coda for that?," hold LT/LR while looking at the man to bring up the dialogue menu and select the code option with X/A.

The oddball man is Dr. Merle, who quickly ingests a tracking device and begins waffling (no pun intended) about his conspiracy theory that the poop of Leonida citizens isn't actually going to the sewers but is instead going to a secret government DNA siphoning center. He then goes to the corporate-controlled bathroom to deposit the tracking device into the federally-controlled sewers, so you can track where Leonida's bowel movements go to the source of the whole operation.

Once Dr Merle is done in the bathroom, follow him to his van outside. Follow his verbal directions to follow the tracker and it'll take you to the sewage treatment plant in Hamlet in Vice-Dale County. Follow the waypoint to park the van on the coast then follow Dr Merle on foot to the plant.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

According to recent reports, when you reach the plant's fence, Dr. Merle begins unlocking a metal gate so that you can get inside and asks you to keep an eye out. Keep an eye on the road on the other side of the gate as a van will soon approach. If the driver stops and asks what you're doing, the best approach is to use the "Defuse" dialogue option to tell the worker you're simply fixing the gate.

It has been revealed that once you're inside the sewage treatment plant ground, you're tasked with finding the tracker. The best approach is to head toward the area highlighted pink on your GTA 6 map until you see the two works chatting. Approach them and, when asked if you are electricians, use the "Lie" dialogue option to go along with their theory. Go through the open metal gate to the left of the works, then slightly right and you'll see a set of double doors. Enter these doors to enter the facility.

Once you get inside Dr. Merle starts to freak out because the tracking device is apparently below your feet, but there's no obvious way to reach it, so he asks you to find a way down. Go up the metal stairs in this room and you'll find a control panel on the platform above. Select Triangle/Y to interact with the panel.

To open the stairs that lead downstairs, all three lights on the left of the control panel need to be turned to green. So, push the buttons next to the two red lights (the middle and bottom ones), to turn them green, then tilt the main lever on the panel. A secret staircase leading downstairs will then open up where Dr.Merle is sitting.

Sources indicate that go down the stairs and you'll enter a room with a large, mysterious-looking chamber. Determined to prove his DNS-siphoning theory is correct, Dr. Merle gets into the chamber– which soon begins to fill with liquid – and asks you to flush him. Press the red button on the control panel in front of the chamber to do so.

Unfortunately, this puts the water authority on your case. They warn over a loudspeaker that the authorities are on their way and that the chamber is highly toxic, so you absolutely should not step inside it. Step inside the chamber and you'll automatically be flushed. You wake up (somehow) outside Jason's House with a notification telling you your max stamina has increased.

The Unexpected History of 'Black Friday'

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1212 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Since the 1950s, Black Friday—once simply known as "the day after Thanksgiving"—has grown into a quasi-holiday in the United States marked by steep discounts, ceaseless shopping, and occasional violence.
  • Sources indicate that while pre-dawn trips to the mall are waning as online shopping grows, in-person shopping on Black Friday is still a big deal in the U.S.—it’s estimated that around 80 million Americans visited a brick-and-mortar store on Black Friday in 2025.
  • According to recent reports, “Black Friday” in the United States originally referred to the start of the Panic of 1869, when the collapse of the price of gold devastated the national economy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since the 1950s, Black Friday—once simply known as "the day after Thanksgiving"—has grown into a quasi-holiday in the United States marked by steep discounts, ceaseless shopping, and occasional violence. But more recently, Black Friday has also metastasized. It's not a day anymore. It's a week, a month, a veritable state of mind. (Speaking of which, check out Lifehacker's Black Friday coverage. We got all the deals, baby!).

Sources indicate that while pre-dawn trips to the mall are waning as online shopping grows, in-person shopping on Black Friday is still a big deal in the U.S.—it’s estimated that around 80 million Americans visited a brick-and-mortar store on Black Friday in 2025. But how did Black Friday come about, and what does it all mean?

According to recent reports, “Black Friday” in the United States originally referred to the start of the Panic of 1869, when the collapse of the price of gold devastated the national economy. “Black Friday” as a description of the day after Thanksgiving dates back to 1951; the term first appeared in the journal Factory Management and Maintenance, where it referred to the number of employees who skipped work on the day after Thanksgiving. Around the same time, the police in Philadelphia and Rochester started informally using “Black Friday” to describe the traffic and crowds that appeared in their cities as shoppers hit the stores on the day after Thanksgiving. The phrase gradually caught on. It was picked up by national press in 1975 when the Fresh York Times used "Black Friday" specifically to describe the day after Thanksgiving and the shopping and sales it brings.

But even before it had a name, Black Friday was a thing. The day after Thanksgiving has been known by merchants as the start of the shopping season since the late 1800s. By the early 20th century, retailers sponsored Thanksgiving Day parades that traditionally ended with an appearance by Santa Claus, as if to say, “Now it’s time to shop for Christmas.” By unspoken agreement among retailers, Christmas-themed advertisements rarely appeared before Thanksgiving in our grandparents’ day. This informal bargain obviously no longer applies.

Referring to a day as “black” traditionally denotes a period of calamity or tragedy, leading some to suggest different names for the day. In the early 1960s, Philadelphia merchants suggested “Big Friday,” a name which did not catch on, leaving retailers with the weak explanation that the “black” in Black Friday refers to the black ink denoting profits in a ledger. Oft-repeated lore suggests that retailers are "in the red" all year, and only start making an annual profit at the end of the year, but big retail chains generally make money all year long.

A more modern matter with the name is that Black Friday sales now last for days or even weeks, beginning in early to mid-November and bleeding over into the following Saturday, Sunday, “Cyber Monday,” Tuesday, and beyond, leading people to say things like, “Do you want to go Black Friday shopping this Sunday?” So far, alternative names like “Five-Day Frenzy” and “The day I get to trample someone to save $8 on a Nespresso” haven’t caught on. But here’s hoping.

Beginning around 2010, an insatiable thirst for profits led many retailers to push the start of Black Friday shopping to Thursday (aka Thanksgiving Day). Kmart opened Thanksgiving morning. Toys R Us opened that night. By 2011, Walmart was opening its doors at 10 p.m. on Thursday. The trend led to widespread backlash, with many Americans appalled that employees were forced to work on Thanksgiving or angry that consumerism was encroaching upon a holiday meant to celebrate colonialism. By 2021, most major retailers had relented and elected to remain closed on Thanksgiving.

In a recent development, the term “Cyber Monday” describes the boost in online retail sales on the Monday after Thanksgiving, sparked by workers returning to the office and getting right to online shopping. The term first appeared on Nov. 28, 2005, in a Shop.org press release entitled “'Cyber Monday’ Swiftly Becoming One of the Biggest Online Shopping Days of the Year," which may be the most influential press release ever written. Since its early 2000s birth, Cyber Monday has become the biggest online shopping day of the year. Americans spent $14.25 billion online on Cyber Monday 2025, according to Adobe Analytics. So is Cyber Monday bigger than Black Friday? Retailers really don't care: Analysts now tend to mash everything into the category of "Black Friday–Cyber Monday" (or even "Cyber Week").

Industry observers note that if all this naked consumerism makes you a little squeamish, you're not alone. Anti-consumerists have named the day after Thanksgiving “Buy Nothing Day,” which you can celebrate by doing charity work, cutting up your credit cards, or simply not purchasing anything. Pioneered by artist Ted Dave and popularized by Adbusters magazine, the first Buy Nothing Day was celebrated in Canada in 1992.

It’s hard to measure the success of the alternative holiday. Both online and brick-and-mortar retail sales have increased sharply since 1992, suggesting Buy Nothing Day’s effect is negligible. On the other hand, maybe big retailers are losing millions because someone on Bluesky reminded you not to shop. Sure.

According to recent reports, depending on how you measure it, Black Friday has resulted in between one and 17 deaths. Jdimytai Damour is the only person killed directly due to a Black Friday sale: The 34-year-old worker was trampled to death by a surging crowd at a Long Island Walmart on Black Friday in 2008. If you include car accidents, shootings, retail worker suicides, and fatal heart attacks, Black Friday’s death toll balloons to 17, with 128 reported injuries.

Black Friday violence has even inspired a horror flick: Eli Roth's 2023 holiday-themed slasher Thanksgiving opens with a hilariously brutal Black Friday riot at a substantial box store, setting off a chain of events that involve a lot of people being murdered by a dude in a Pilgrim mask.

According to recent reports, I mean, yeah, of course. Critics of Black Friday point out that there are arguably better times to buy a new TV (like the week before the Super Bowl), not to mention plenty of other goods. Savings from Black Friday shopping are often illusory—massive-ticket “doorbuster” items generally sell out swiftly, leaving behind goods that are, by and large, priced the same as they would be at any other time of year. Some retailers even mark up products ahead of Black Friday so the discounts look bigger. If you're buying online, your browser history, location, and cart contents can tweak the prices you see on Black Friday, as they can on any other day.

In a recent development, yet despite protest holidays, the unpleasantness of shopping when stores are overcrowded, and the frustration of hunting for bargains that often aren't that great to begin with, Black Friday stubbornly remains an unofficial holiday, celebrated by over 100 million Americans in one way or another. What that claims about our country's relationship with capitalism is unclear, but personally, I’m going to continue my own day-after-Thanksgiving tradition of eating pie for breakfast and thinking about going for a walk, but then watching The Quick and the Dead instead. I'm not protesting anything; I just don't need the hassle.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that spoilers for Sunrise on the Reaping are ahead! You can catch The Hunger Games prequel in theaters now.

Ever since the novel Sunrise on the Reaping came out, there’d been rumblings about Jennifer Lawrence, Josh Hutcherson and Woody Harrelson reprising their Hunger Games roles in the book-to-screen adaptation of the prequel. Now, the film is out on the 2026 movie schedule, the original Katniss, Peeta and Haymitch came back, and watching their scene together at the end of the movie made me emotional.

I really think it’ll stick with me too, and as I continue to be sappy about seeing these actors together again as these beloved characters, Josh Hutcherson explained how it all came together.

Before we get into how these cameos happened, let’s talk about what happened on the big screen.

At the end of Sunrise on the Reaping, we see Haymitch go back to District 12, and he learns that his mom and brother have died. Not long after that, Lenore Dove dies too after eating poisoned candy. Defeated by all of this, Haymitch isolates himself in Victors' Village, and we start to see him transform into the cynical man we meet in The Hunger Games as he watches kids die year after year in the games.

In a recent development, then, there’s a major time jump from Haymitch’s first lonely years at home to a time post-Mockingjay. At that point, Woody Harrelson takes over to play the victor, and we see him with Jennifer Lawrence’s Katniss and Josh Hutcherson’s Peeta as they gather together. Notably, it’s clear they’re finally living in a world with no Hunger Games. They all seem at peace, and after their interaction, Haymitch goes to sit with the geese.

It has been revealed that overall, it’s a hopeful ending to a truly tragic tale, because it shows that even though it took decades, eventually, the games stopped. And it will stick with me, because knowing Haymitch found his people and was able to live on happily with them after everything he had to endure makes me incredibly happy.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Plus, seeing Jennifer Lawrence back as Katniss and Josh Hutcherson return as Peeta meant the world to me, a gal who literally grew up on The Hunger Games books and movies. Now, how did the original band get back together for this? Hutcherson answered the question on Happy Sad Confused, explaining that it was a pretty significant secret for a while:.

I heard nothing until the day Francis Lawrence called me in maybe early summer of last year or something. And he called me and was like, ‘I have top secret information I need to share with you.’ And my heart dropped because I was like, ‘I don’t know what’s going to happen. This could be literally anything.’.

Hutcherson quickly learned it was Sunrise on the Reaping, and the director was also quick to tell him that Lawrence and Harrelson had already noted yes:.

[He told me] he’d read the manuscript and that, at the end of the film, we appear as our current aged selves. And he was like, ‘I talked with Jen. I talked with Woody. They’re down. Are you down?’ And I was like, ‘I’ve been waiting for this day for 15 years.’.

When Hutcherson was asked what his texts with Lawrence looked like after they learned about this, he remarked it was “just all caps.” They really were so excited to reunite for this.

Industry observers note that then, the trio went to Germany for a week; they shot for “four hours,” according to the Peeta actor, and then they got to “hang out” and “catch up.” Many months later, they reunited for the Sunrise premiere too. So, all around, it sounds like it was a lovely experience.

According to recent reports, overall, I don’t think Sunrise on the Reaping works without this last scene. We need that sliver of hope that highlights that everything Haymitch went through ultimately led to a good outcome. It also brings the story full-circle and all the way back to the first characters (and actors) we got to see in this universe.

  • Kurabayashi initially worked as a programmer on smaller titles at Taito, including early 2.5D fighting game Fighters' Impact (later localised as VS.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As announced in a statement by Arika president Akira Nishitani (and translated by Time Extension, thank you), Akira Kurabayashi, a director at the combined dev/publishing studio and a creator whose work spans three decades and several genres, sadly passed away as a result of heart failure late last week.

Kurabayashi initially worked as a programmer on smaller titles at Taito, including early 2.5D fighting game Fighters' Impact (later localised as VS. in America). He then moved to Arika in 1996 and continued his work in 2.5D fighters with the Street Fighter EX series, a subseries which took the originator of the fighting game genre into the third dimension for the first time. While that subseries didn't last long, its spiritual successor Fighting EX Layer made waves in 2018, bringing back original characters from SFEX and even including Fatal Fury's Terry Bogard.

Fighting EX Layer started out as an April Fools' joke back in 2017, but the reaction to the trailer from fans who missed the SFEX series convinced Arika to bring the series back, even without the Capcom IP. The final result is an interesting 2.5D fighter that combines conventional mechanics, such as magic series combos and supers, with the unique (for better and worse) Gougi system, where of in-match perks are chosen from a deck of cards at roundstart. I had a good time playing it for its systems (and Terry is very fun in it), but the Gougi system brought to mind Street Fighter x Tekken's infamous paid Gem debacle, which no one should be reminded of. Anyway. In addition to 2.5D fighters, Kurabayashi also contributed to Tetris: The Grandmaster, Tetris 99, PAC-MAN 99, and ARIKA's collaboration with SNK in the form of their 'SNK Revamp Project'.

Nishitani gave a few personal words towards Kurabayashi in the statement:.

Industry observers note that "We are deeply saddened to have lost a dear colleague who has created numerous works with us and supported Arika for many years. We express our heartfelt respect and gratitude for his immense achievements to date, and we will cherish and carry on the skills, experience, and attitude toward game development that he left behind. I would like to express my deepest gratitude for the kindness you demonstrated us during their lifetime, and I respectfully pray for the repose of their soul.".

Condolences to Kurabayashi's family.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Like many major brands, Xbox is finding all sorts of ways to associate with the biggest game launch of the year: Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • In a recent development, as pointed out by multiple people on social media, the Xbox Wire post titled 'How to Get Ready for November 19' is one all about celebrating the massive release day of GTA 6, and helping players find ways to maximise their time with their Xbox consoles.
  • "Birthdays, anniversaries, and holidays have come and gone, but this day belongs to you and your Xbox console," the post reads, stopping short of saying why the day is notable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Like many major brands, Xbox is finding all sorts of ways to associate with the biggest game launch of the year: Grand Theft Auto 6. Unlike indie publisher Devolver Digital, however, Xbox has cleverly avoided ever mentioning GTA 6 directly in its marketing campaigns for GTA 6.

In a recent development, as pointed out by multiple people on social media, the Xbox Wire post titled 'How to Get Ready for November 19' is one all about celebrating the massive release day of GTA 6, and helping players find ways to maximise their time with their Xbox consoles. Despite that, it does not mention GTA 6 by name a single time.

"Birthdays, anniversaries, and holidays have come and gone, but this day belongs to you and your Xbox console," the post reads, stopping short of saying why the day is notable. "We can hardly believe it's almost here, either.".

According to recent reports, one day prior, Xbox Wire partnered with DJ Khaled to create custom doctor's notes for players to submit to their employers to take the day off. Why would you want to take 19th November off? Because you're apparently having "a serious case of Vitamin G deficiency".

Industry observers note that going even further back, Xbox revealed a custom-made Series X console it called X-Bite, which is a large, sculpted alligator that swallowed a Series X console. Why? Because "this November, Xbox is heading to Florida - home to incredible wildlife, unforgettable places, and every now and then, stories you have to see to believe.".

Florida, of course, is the real-world US state GTA 6's Leonida is based on, but in keeping with the theme of not referring to the game - or its made-up state - directly, the blog does not.

It has been revealed that now, Xbox has directly named GTA 6 in places, but only when, seemingly, the post is about factual information. This Xbox Wire post reiterates GTA 6's Xbox Cloud streaming availability, and this one is a look-ahead at games launching the following week on Xbox. But that's about the extent of what you can expect.

So what's going on here? The simple guess is that PlayStation has a co-marketing deal with Rockstar, meaning no other console platform gets to use GTA 6's name in marketing. Sony is allowed to make custom, GTA 6-themed consoles, branded, limited-edition DualSense controllers and blaster the game all over the PS Blog, social media, and even change the PS App's icon colour to match the hue of GTA 6's.

Sources indicate that this is all too similar to when, each year, various brands encourage you to buy their products to be ready for The Big Game, which is very distinct from the Super Bowl happening on the same day. Like Xbox, those brands simply don't have the rights to the real thing.

Sources indicate that GTA 6 is available now on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. In Eurogamer's five-star review, Chris Tapsell wrote, "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that.".

Sources indicate that this is Terminally Online: PC Gamer's very own MMO column. Every other week, I'll be sharing my thoughts on the genre, interviewing fellow MMO-heads like me, taking a deep-dive into mechanics we've all taken for granted, and, occasionally, bringing in guest writers to talk about their MMO of choice.

World of Warcraft: Forever's done a lot of things for me over the past couple of weeks—it's given me a deeper appreciation for oldschool MMO quest design, it's wowed me with some genuinely impressive upcoming lighting technology, and it's… ugh, it's made me so friendly.

According to recent reports, mind, I wouldn't say I'm unkind when I play MMOs, but I am a solo player by habit. I'll have a guild, friends I roleplay with, sure. But I'm very rarely striking up conversations with people in-game—all of that typically happens in Discord. And yet, here I am in WoW forever, trying to emphatically start conversations with goddamn everyone I meet.

In a recent development, and it's in part because of how much of a bastard the game is. I don't think Classic is a particularly difficult videogame—I've even gotten my warrior from level 1 to, at the time of writing, 56 as fury, a spec typically considered trash for levelling. And it's been fine, I've just minded my pulls and levelled first aid.

Recent findings suggest that but it is a known fact that vanilla WoW quests are just easier when you group up with people. Part of this is because players are a force multiplier—many classes have group buffs, and not having to worry about health with a healer present means that you can pull swathes of enemies and melt them down easily.

In a recent development, and so I've been doing that. I've been grouping with people, and they've been grouping with me, and… oh, god, we've been talking to each other.

I don't know if I just happen to have a lucky propensity for drawing in nice folks, but my levelling journey has been dappled with some of the chillest people you'll ever meet. People hanging around to help you finish quests they've already completed is so common it's almost standard.

In one instance, a shadow priest carried me through multiple elite quests in Stranglethorn Vale—they needed to do 'em too, sure, but they actively went out of their way to show me where I could get a couple.

Keep up to date with the most key stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

According to recent reports, there is a real, tangible sense of camaraderie in the game right now, one that's yet to be grinded to the marrow by the efficiency-laden tasks of Mythic+ or a seasonal system. But it's also one borne of how long everything takes. When you've already spent 10 minutes jogging to a quest, what's another five to help a stranger out?

Recent findings suggest that it is, to put it plainly, the opposite of what I'd expected after years of playing far more modern MMOs. I'm even way ahead of the curve of the general population level-wise, and I'm still meeting these relaxed, generous folks. People who'll offer up scraps of a treasure map that's dropping from the pirates we're grinding for free, rather than being a mercenary about it and selling them on the auction house.

Recent findings suggest that moreover, it is infectious. I've been handing mana potions to people. I've been sticking around to help out with quests—in a recent Zul'farrak run, a dungeon I was only doing twice because I'd missed that it was required for the Sunken Temple questline, our tank had simply atrocious luck collecting troll tempers for a quest (you need 20 of them, and they don't drop often).

Industry observers note that not just myself, but another player in the same situation all stuck around for about 20 minutes just to help them out. When they thanked us, I, saccharine and glowing with the spirit of a reformed Grinch, said: "No worries, bud, if you wanna live in a village you've gotta be a villager sometimes.".

Recent findings suggest that in short, Forever's turned me into a significant, fluffy, golden-haired dog. The kind you meet in a park that bounds up to you with its stupid tongue wagging out. All that oldschool game design and camaraderie has, as it turns out, been a complete antidote to my hermetic ways. And while my street cred as a tough, solemn badass might never recover, I'm glad to be taking my time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that for the past six years, the team at RPS have got together to pick what we consider to be the best 100 games you can play on PC. There's very little science involved, and we try not to get too hung up on what games should make the cut. From year to year, our rankings and choices vary wildly as the formation and tastes of the team changes.

Recent findings suggest that however, our definitive list isn't always met with a chorus of approval and cheers of 'Hear, hear!', "'Well done!', and 'Couldn't have said it better myself!', so we also have the RPS 100: Reader Edition. This is your chance to submit your ten favourite PC games of all time. Your votes will be tallied up with all the other submissions from our other readers and we will produce a list of the community's top 100.

We've just finished revealing what we right now consider to be the Best PC games of all time and now it's your turn.

Recent findings suggest that using this very Google Form you can submit up to ten votes for your favourite PC games of all time. I will then tally them up with all the other votes from RPS's readers and produce a list of the community's top 100.

Now, a note on scoring. The game you put in 10th place will be awarded one point, 9th place will be worth two, 8th place will be worth three, and so on until you reach your top pick, which will be worth ten points. Please write the full game name (and include the year of release if there are multiple titles in a series with the same name, such as Doom (1993) and Doom (2016)). If in doubt, check how the game is titled on Steam.

Industry observers note that last year, I implemented a change to create a greater variety of games on the list. I combined series scores, so if one reader voted for Civilization IV and another voted for Civilization VI, the scores of both were combined and the entry would be for the Civilization series. I also shared the breakdown of the votes for each title in the entry, so you could see which was most popular within the series.

According to recent reports, I will be doing the same again this year, as we saw a lot more games that wouldn't have made the cut otherwise. However, I will try to do a better job of separating out games that are very different from one another even if they are in the same series. Warcraft 3 and World of Warcraft are both Warcraft games, but, admittedly, they aren't similar games. I would ask for some leeway on this, though, as not every example is clear cut. Should Alpha Centauri be counted among the Civilization games? Are Final Fantasy XIV and Final Fantasy Tactics - The Ivalice Chronicles truly worlds away from the other games in the Final Fantasy series?

This does also mean that one-shot games can struggle to compete against games which are part of longrunning series. After all, Crimson Skies isn't just competing against Microsoft Flight Simulator (2020), it is competing against votes for any and all Microsoft Flight Simulator games ever released. Unfortunately, this is a cost of the system, but I prefer the variety that comes from seeing more games represented instead of several separate entries for games within the same series.

It has been revealed that we also invite you to tell us why you've chosen each game. This is entirely voluntary, you can simply enter the game titles if you would prefer. However, I'll choose a selection of what readers have mentioned about winning games so we can better understand why the RPS community loves these games. Try not to write any more than 100 words. If you have more to say you can always drop it in the comments of the list when we publish it at the end of the year.

To cast your votes, please make sure you complete this form by 5pm GMT on Sunday, December 6th.

Thanks again, and happy voting!

Liverpool are ready to let a long-serving stalwart leave Anfield for free in 2027, according to one insider.

The last player standing from the tail end of Brendan Rodgers’ managerial reign, Joe Gomez is now into his 12th season with the Reds, albeit that he’s been consigned to a backup role thus far under Andoni Iraola.

The 29-year-old has featured for just 259 minutes across our 16 matches so far in this campaign, more than half of which have come in the Carabao Cup (Transfermarkt), and as it stand he’ll be out of contract in seven months’ time.

Ex-Manchester United chief scout Mick Brown has claimed that Liverpool sporting director Julian Ward has already decided that the club’s longest-serving current player won’t be offered a upcoming deal, with injury problems not helping the defender’s case.

He told Football Insider: “Liverpool have already decided they’re going to let Joe Gomez leave. He doesn’t have much of a role to play at the moment, he’s not starting games at right-back even despite their injuries, and he isn’t competing for a centre-back position.

“His injuries are always a concern as well. They don’t think he can start games consistently, and all of these issues stack up eventually.

“It would be a surprise to me if they were to offer him a latest contract, especially when you consider they’re going to be looking to bring in new defenders at some stage.

“If he hasn’t played much this season, that’s not going to change with fresh players coming in, so I expect he’ll be allowed to look at what other options might be available.”.

Recent findings suggest that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Ward could be quite busy with contract renewals over the next few months, with Alisson Becker, Virgil van Dijk and Alexis Mac Allister reportedly all in line for prospective upcoming deals.

Whereas that trio are virtually guaranteed to start, though, Gomez usually has to rely on substitute appearances or heavy squad rotation for domestic cup games, and it’s not implausible that he could be allowed to depart on a free transfer next summer.

If that is indeed his fate, he’ll be assured of a raucous send-off at Anfield on the final day of the season, with his popularity among the fan base unmistakably evident by the roar which greeted his successful penalty in the Carabao Cup shootout triumph over Chelsea last month.

As Lewis Steele rightly said, the 29-year-old ‘very rarely puts a foot wrong’ whenever he’s called upon, and even if he isn’t getting much game-time, we don’t doubt that he’s imparting some invaluable advice to the young defenders at Liverpool who can learn so much from him.

It has been revealed that if this is to be Gomez’s last campaign with the Reds, all we ask is that he does finally, finally get his first goal for the club during regulation time. You’d be very hard pressed to find a more popular goalscorer if that moment were to happen!

  • According to recent reports, one of the more controversial aspects of the production of You Can See Everything was Evans negotiating a payout with execs from A24 and the movie's co-directors, Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it turns out Elizabeth Holmes’ partner, Billy Evans, did successfully manage a payout from the producers of You Can See Everything, which has been crushing it on the 2026 movie schedule. However, the money isn’t going to him or Holmes. Instead, it’s going to charity. The details are still a little murky, but we do have more understanding of what went down after the scene in the movie where he brings it up and the card at the end that explains he changed his mind and wasn’t going to profit from the movie. Given how massive a box office hit ($89 million and counting) the A24 release has been, it's probably a nice chunk of change. So what is going on? Here’s what we know.

According to recent reports, one of the more controversial aspects of the production of You Can See Everything was Evans negotiating a payout with execs from A24 and the movie's co-directors, Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim. The scene, which sees Evans asking for money after Holmes has left the room, has been a topic of conversation among fans of the film. Even lawyers have chimed in on how it could affect the judgment against Holmes, who owes somewhere north of $400 million in restitution after her conviction on fraud crimes.

Industry observers note that in the scene, everyone agrees that Evans (and presumably Holmes) will be paid for their appearances. Then, at the end, a card appears informing the audience that Evans backed off this deal and wouldn’t be paid. Now, a new report in The Hollywood Reporter has clarified it. According to the article, Evans is earning money on the backend, but that money is reportedly going to a children’s charity. The article did not specify which charity.

It has been revealed that the outlet also confirmed with A24 that a deal had been struck, but neither the outlet’s sources nor A24 revealed how much the charity would be getting or what percentage of the backend was negotiated. The film is closing in on $100 million at the box office, and it's sure to earn more when it hits VOD sometime in the near future (the exact date is still not confirmed). That’s to say nothing about whatever money the film will earn when it moves to HBO Max, likely in early 2027.

This is yet another saga in a movie that is full of intrigue both on-screen and off. It is also another wrinkle in trying to determine what is true and what is not. That question is at the core of the movie, and it seems even now, weeks after its release and years after Evans and Holmes were filmed before she reported to prison in 2023. That question is still lingering in every aspect. I’ve remarked before that this movie is like an onion, and this is one more layer getting peeled away, but it’s only offering up another layer that is just as fascinating.

Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

Nvidia's latest graphics card driver appears to be unnecessarily writing to PC SSDs, something that's dumb, annoying and definitely warrants reverting

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (357 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ooh, an Nvidia-related story that isn't about their now former CEO allegedly getting amorous with someone.
  • As noted by PC Gamer, reports of driver 621.24 writing more than it should to SSDs have popped up across various forums and Reddit.
  • In a recent development, some instances of the bug, which doesn't appear to be affecting everyone, have the driver writing up to 30GB every hour.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ooh, an Nvidia-related story that isn't about their now former CEO allegedly getting amorous with someone. I wonder what it's abou-oh. Oh no. It looks like Nvidia's latest GeForce driver, 621.24, is needlessly writing vast amounts of data to PC SSDs.

As noted by PC Gamer, reports of driver 621.24 writing more than it should to SSDs have popped up across various forums and Reddit.

In a recent development, some instances of the bug, which doesn't appear to be affecting everyone, have the driver writing up to 30GB every hour. For context, it'd take a bugged driver writing that much thousands of hours to break a gaming SSD with a typical endurance rating in the hundreds of terabytes. However, that doesn't mean this is anything less than a pretty bad bug. As such, reverting to the previous driver, 621.01, is a good idea if you're on 621.24 and suspect it of writing chunks of gigabytes to your SSD.

In a recent development, in order to check if that's going on, open task manager, head to the 'details' tab, right click on the column header, click 'select columns', select 'I/O write bytes' from the menu of check boxes that brings up, then look for 'NVDisplay.Container.exe'. The number next that exe is in bytes, so you'll need to do a bit of maths to work out if it's writing mere MB or globs of GB.

Bizarrely, the affected 621.24 driver still hasn't been pulled by Nvidia as of writing, meaning it can still be downloaded by people who might not be aware of any problems and think 'ooh, haven't checked I'm on the latest driver in a while.' The driver was released on November 12th, so it's not a brand upcoming arrival that the firm just haven't had a chance to look into yet.

Here's hoping that it is fixed or replaced ASAP, if it hasn't been by the time you read this. AMD look to have dealt with a similar concern recently, and I'd like to think driver updates across all cards aren't going to be some form of permanent Russian roulette going forwards.

GTA 6 developers at Rockstar are worried about being laid off after shipping "the biggest game of all time"

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, rockstar has successfully shipped Grand Theft Auto 6, after years of work and more than a billion dollars spent.
  • In a recent development, but that may not be enough to prevent layoffs at Rockstar, some people working within the studio fear.
  • According to recent reports, "After the significant day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it's hard not to worry about what the future holds," Uriarte wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, rockstar has successfully shipped Grand Theft Auto 6, after years of work and more than a billion dollars spent. GTA 6 is already one of the highest-rated games ever - Eurogamer awarded it five stars in our GTA 6 review - and it's expected to be among the most successful, best-selling games ever.

In a recent development, but that may not be enough to prevent layoffs at Rockstar, some people working within the studio fear. Nestor Uriarte, an animation programmer at Rockstar North, wrote about their concern for their job and those of their colleagues in an article on The Guardian.

According to recent reports, "After the significant day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it's hard not to worry about what the future holds," Uriarte wrote. "It claims a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off. But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.".

Recent findings suggest that uriarte's piece comes as Rockstar staff's efforts to establish a union reach a critical point. A tribunal between the studio and fired IWBG union members just concluded, though the verdict may not arrive for many weeks or months.

It has been revealed that rockstar's UK studios are at the moment voting on recognising an official Rockstar workers union. Uriarte is in support of it and has urged colleagues to vote in favour of it. Results of that vote are expected today.

"Winning union recognition would be a huge step forward in securing a meaningful say over our conditions at Rockstar, but its significance would reach far beyond that," Uriarte pointed out.

"As one of the biggest and most influential game studios in the world, what happens here could open the door for other workers across the UK to imagine an alternative future for the industry - one in which workers' voices are taken into account more.".

Across its 12 offices around the world, Rockstar's headcount grew to 4,711 during GTA 6's development - double its size when it released Red Dead Redemption 2.

Sources indicate that as popular and profitable as Rockstar's games are, the company has initiated layoffs in the past after shipping a major project. While there's no way of knowing whether the same is going to happen for GTA 6, the justifiable concerns - given the current state of the industry - are there. According to the ASGC Games Industry Layoffs Tracker, more than 12,000 developers have lost their jobs this year so far, up from more than 9,000 people last year.

Beats has a long history of making on-ear headphones that stand with the plushest and best-sounding cans on the market. As early Black Friday deals get underway, it's a great time to upgrade: Walmart has discounted the Beats Solo 4 by more than 65%, to $69 (originally $199.99); the sale applies to the Gray and Sandstone variants.

These headphones don’t have ANC, just passive isolation, but they still deliver solid sound, comfort, and strong battery life. They use physical controls and support one-touch pairing with most Apple devices, as well as hands-free Siri.A The Solo 4 headphones are compatible with Bluetooth 5.3 and work with the AAC and SBC codecs. The headphones last around 50 hours per charge (about 10 hours longer than their predecessor), and 10 minutes of charging gives you around five hours of playback, with a full recharge taking approximately two hours. For $69, the Beats Solo 4 headphones are a compact and well-equipped option for casual listening, with long battery life and that classic Beats aesthetic.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As reported by The Shanghai Observer and Automaton, authorities in Shanghai have arrested 13 people and seized an untold number of unauthorized model kits and figures based on pop culture properties like Final Fantasy. The cops were reportedly put on the trail by a suspect Tifa Lockheart figurine.

Police in Fengxian, a district of Shanghai, began receiving complaints in June. The Shanghai Observer demonstrated pictures comparing a Play Arts Kai (Square Enix's premium figure line) Tifa with a seemingly less articulated counterpart in the same outfit. Reading through machine translation, it sounds like customers in the area bought these figures online expecting the genuine article.

The leader of the operation reportedly commissioned a Guangzhou factory to produce the false Tifa and her ilk. They even sold some figures at higher prices than the genuine article, offering added accessories or features not available in the official product.

I'm of two minds about this, personally: I'm generally pro-kitbashing, selling custom figures, and using proxies in trading card games. In the face of some seriously inflated pricing from official merch lines, bootlegs can often be more enticing than the real deal, particularly if they offer features you can't get from official products⁠—the added customization options from this arrested vendor actually sound weirdly pro-consumer.

But it certainly appears, at least from The Shanghai Observer's reporting, that these suspect figures were being presented as the genuine article to customers. Paired with the increased price vs. official merch, and I find myself soured on the whole operation. It may seem small and silly, but as we endure the Golden Age of Scams, it's weirdly nice to see scammers face some consequences somewhere.
